Hi Soojin / Monica —

Quick note: our GA for feature set A is moving up two weeks to 2026-09-15. Our internal load tests indicate peak inference QPS will be ~3.2x what we originally signed up for in the first 4 weeks post-GA. We know this is a tight window, but OrbitLane cannot tolerate degraded latency on day 1 — it’s core to their demo to partners.

Can Redwood provide a temporary uplift or re-prioritization for the first 30 days? If we can get a short-term 2x uplift on dedicated capacity (or a higher-priority tranche) that would cover us while we optimize prompts and caching.

Attached: orbitlane_usage_report_q3.csv (sample traces + p50/p95 from staging).

Appreciate a fast yes/no and any options.

—Jared

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: OrbitLane launch — capacity question

Soojin — quick technical assessment after a sync with infra ops:

Summary: A 2x uplift for 30 days is technically possible but will require:
- reserving an additional tranche of 8 A100 GPU-equivalent slots for the region (us-west) for the 30-day window, or
- alternative: a dynamic priority lane that gives OrbitLane preemptible headroom (lower cost) but with a preemption policy that only triggers under critical congestion.

Trade-offs and risk:
- Full reserved uplift (8 slots) guarantees latency but consumes capacity that might otherwise be allocated to existing Reserved customers (risk: entitlement disputes).
- Priority lane reduces guaranteed throughput and is complex to explain to customer, but it won’t block long-term committed customers.

Estimated ops work: 4–6 engineer-hours to provision + 6–8 hours to validate routing and KV cache policies. I attached a quick capacity plan and allocation sketch.

Attachments: temp_capacity_plan_orbitlane_v1.xlsx (proposed slot schedule + fallback routing).

If leadership greenlights a temporary reserved uplift we should also:
- create a short SLA amendment (Monica),
- schedule a 48-hour cutover test 1 week before GA (SRE + OrbitLane),
- include a post-30-day rollback plan and cost reconciliation.

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: OrbitLane launch — capacity question

Thanks Karthik — commercial take below.

Option A — Short reserved uplift (recommended for OrbitLane demo-critical launch):
- 30-day reserved tranche: +8 A100-equivalent slots in us-west, billed at committed reserved rate pro-rated for 30 days.
- One-time operational surcharge for provisioning and validation: $6,500.
- Require a signed SLA amendment confirming the uplift window and rollback date.

Option B — Priority lane (lower cost, conditional throughput):
- No reserved slots; routing policy assigns higher priority but preemptible capacity during congestion.
- Lower cost to customer, but we cannot guarantee p95 under extreme fleet contention.

Monetary impact to Redwood: reserving 8 slots reduces available headroom for other commitments; this is manageable short-term but will require leadership sign-off if any overlapping reserved customers exist in the same tranche.

Requesting Vivek’s approval to proceed with Option A as an exception for OrbitLane given strategic value and partner references (they’re part of a channel portfolio). If Vivek approves, Monica and I will get the SLA amendment redline ready and loop legal.

Attachments: sla_amendment_draft_orbitlane.docx (initial template).

—Monica
Senior Sales Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: OrbitLane launch — urgent capacity split & temporary uplift request

Hi Jared / Priya —

Thanks for the quick data and patience. Internal recommendation: we can offer a short-term reserved uplift (Option A) of +8 A100-equivalent slots in us-west for the period 2026-09-15 to 2026-10-15. High-level terms:

- Reserved uplift: +8 slots, pro-rated reserved billing for 30 days.
- Ops surcharge: $6,500 (one-time).
- Pre-production cutover test: 48-hour window 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-08 (SRE + Redwood).
- Rollback: automatic revert to baseline on 2026-10-15 00:00 UTC unless both parties agree to extend.
- Requires a signed SLA amendment and acceptance of the operational surcharge.

If OrbitLane agrees, Monica will send a redlined SLA amendment and an invoice for the surcharge. Please confirm by EOD tomorrow so we can reserve capacity and schedule the cutover test.

Cc’ing Vivek for awareness; he’s flagged this as an exception and will weigh in if overlapping reserved customers are impacted.

Best,
Soojin
